passages.provision_quote: The hourly minimum wage for fast food restaurant employees shall be twenty dollars ($20) per hour, effective April 1, 2024. Thereafter, the council may establish, pursuant to this subdivision, minimum wages for fast food restaurant employees that take effect on an annual basis, beginning on January 1, 2025.
passages.note: Chaptered text prints the operative wage provision and the council's discretionary annual-increase cap, but names no voter.

rows.reasoning: Wicks voted Aye on AB 1228 (2023-2024), which sets a $20 hourly wage for fast food restaurant employees and provides that "Thereafter, the council may establish, pursuant to this subdivision, minimum wages for fast food restaurant employees that take effect on an annual basis, beginning on January 1, 2025." That shows she favors raising a wage floor, but it does not separate "tie it to the cost of living, so it rises automatically each year without new legislation" from "adjust it only when lawmakers vote to": the increase is discretionary ("may establish") and capped at the lesser of 3.5 percent or CPI-W, so it is neither automatic indexing nor an adjustment reserved to lawmakers. It is also a single-sector wage rather than the general wage floor the rungs order, so it cannot fix a rung on its own.
